name: Issue Log
purpose: Records and monitors issues. An issue is a current condition or situation that could affect the project objectives, such as a point in dispute or under discussion, opposing views, or a risk event that has happened and must now be dealt with. It is created at the start of the project and kept up to date throughout.

starts.cite: Book of Forms form 3.1, PDF page 176 (printed page 165)

receives_from.what: a risk event that has occurred can become an issue (prose: issues can arise from a risk event that has occurred and must now be dealt with); which form carries the event is a reading, the prose names no form
new issues identified by a team member in the reporting period; Table 4.1 says they should be recorded in the issue log as well
new issues identified in the reporting period; Table 4.2 says they should be recorded in the issue log as well

alignment.what_must_agree: an issue that grew out of a realised risk must tell the same story as that risk's entry in the risk register (the prose says issues can arise from a risk event that has occurred; the book gives no further rule)
a decision taken to resolve an issue must not contradict the decision log (overlap not spelled out in the book; reading from the Alignment list)
a lesson drawn from an issue must match the issue's final resolution (overlap not spelled out in the book; reading from the Alignment list)

elements.guidance: A unique identifier for each issue.
The type or category of issue, for example stakeholder issue, technical issue or conflict.
A detailed description of the issue.
The priority, for example urgent, high, medium or low.
Which project objectives the issue affects and how much.
The person assigned to resolve the issue.
The date by which the issue needs to be resolved, that is a target date; the book describes it as a deadline, not as the date the issue was closed.
Clarifying comments about the issue, its resolution or any other field.

tailoring: Add information on the source of the issue.
Add a field naming the stakeholders who are affected by the issue or should help resolve it.

decisions.notes: Urgent, high, medium or low are the book's examples; no scale or threshold is stated in the book.

decisions.decision: By when the issue must be resolved
Which objectives the issue affects and by how much
Whether the issue is still open

notes: The blank form (PDF page 178, printed page 167) prints two banks of columns: the first bank is Issue ID, Type, Issue Description, Priority, Impact on Objectives; the second bank is Responsible Party, Status, Res. Date, Final Resolution, Comments, and row N of bank 2 continues row N of bank 1. Table 3.1 calls the first column ID and the date Resolution date; the blank form wins. The prose does not say which documents the issue log provides information to (not stated in the book).
